Now, from 2 June to 16 June, there are 14 days,

⇒ 14/7 = 2 weeks + 0 odd days.

So, 16 June 1996 = Sunday + 0 = Sunday

Thus, on 16 June 1996, the day was 'Sunday'

questions.question: How many countries are part of SAARC?
questions.solution:

• Its Secretariat was established in **Kathmandu, Nepal,** on January 17, 1987.
 
• SAARC comprises eight member countries:** Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.**
 
• The objectives of SAARC include enhancing the welfare of the people of South Asia, improving their standard of living, fostering economic growth, social advancement, and cultural enrichment in the region.
 
• SAARC also aims to ensure every individual has the opportunity to lead a dignified life and realize their full potential.
 
• Additionally, SAARC endeavours to strengthen collaboration with other developing nations and to engage with international and regional organizations sharing similar goals and objectives.

• To address the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, SAARC devised and enacted a regional emergency fund totaling approximately 22 million USD.
 
• This fund aims to enhance cooperation among member states in combatting the pandemic's effects and supporting collective efforts towards recovery and resilience.

questions.question: Chaitrual and Phulaich are the festivals of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chaitrual and Phulaich** are the festivals of **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• Chaitrual is a widely celebrated festival in the Sirmaur area, occurring during the Chaitra month's bright fortnight on a specific day.
 
• During this occasion, households clear and adorn their walls, painting them and embellishing them with depictions of male animals and crops, symbolizing abundance.
 
• It is also referred to as the **"festival of pictures."**
 
• In the Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh, the Phulaich Festival, alternatively known as Ookayand Festival or Ukyam Festival, is observed in September.
 
• The term 'Oo' denotes 'flowers,' while 'Kayang' signifies 'festival,' making Phulaich synonymous with the** 'festival of flowers.'**
 
• On the 16th day of the Hindu month of 'Bhadrapada,' ten Rajputs from the village venture to the high hills to gather select flowers from the blooming season of wildflowers in the upper regions of Kinnaur district.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Himachal Pradesh **is a state located in the northern region of India.
 
• Nestled in the Western Himalayas, Himachal Pradesh is one of the thirteen mountain states and boasts a rugged landscape marked by numerous peaks and extensive river systems.
 
• As the northernmost state in India, it shares borders with the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh to the north.
 
• To the west lie the states of Punjab, while Haryana borders it to the southwest and Uttarakhand to the southeast.
 
• Additionally, Himachal Pradesh has a narrow boundary with Uttar Pradesh to the south. Towards the east, the state shares an international border with the Tibet Autonomous Region in China.

• **The National Institute of Kathak Dance**, commonly known as Kathak Kendra, is the foremost institution dedicated to the classical dance form of Kathak.
 
• As a unit of the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance, and Drama, it is located in New Delhi.
 
• Established in 1964, Kathak Kendra primarily focuses on Kathak training but also offers courses in Hindustani classical music (vocal) and Pakhawaj and Tabla. With the decline of royal patronage after India gained independence in 1947, Kathak exponents and gurus faced challenges. Many began teaching privately.
 
• Under the patronage of the Awadh state, Lachhu Maharaj relocated to Bombay, while his brother, Shambhu Maharaj, along with his nephew, moved to Delhi in 1955.

• Following Shambhu Maharaj's passing in 1970, his nephew, Birju Maharaj, a renowned Kathak dancer and guru, assumed leadership roles at the institution.
 
• Birju Maharaj's tenure witnessed a transformation in Kathak performance, adapting it from intimate gatherings to large-scale productions in modern theaters.
 
• He introduced several acclaimed ballets during this period, gradually transitioning Kathak from a solo dance form to one that embraced group performances.

__
 
• **Self-help Groups (SHGs) **are informal associations formed by people with similar economic and social backgrounds to collectively address their challenges and enhance their quality of life.
 
• These groups are typically self-managed and operated by their members. Individuals often come together with the assistance of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) or government agencies to address common issues and uplift their living standards.
 
• The roots of SHGs in India can be traced back to the establishment of the Self-Employed Women’s Association (SEWA) in 1972.
 
• Even earlier instances of self-organization existed, such as the formation of the women’s wing of the Textile Labour Association (TLA) of Ahmedabad in 1954, aimed at training women from mill worker families in various skills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• To foster the growth of the SHG movement, the government should create an enabling environment and act as a facilitator and promoter. Additionally, expanding the SHG movement to credit-deficient areas like Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and the North-Eastern states is crucial for broader socioeconomic development.

questions.question: Use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation is referred to as ______.
questions.solution:

• It involves higher levels of input and output per unit of agricultural land area compared to extensive farming practices.
 
• In contrast, extensive farming involves cultivating large farms with relatively smaller inputs, such as cash and labor, and is typically practiced in regions with extensive land and sparse population.

• **In a Capitalistic farming system,** farming activities are directed and managed by individual entrepreneurs who exercise control over the agricultural processes.

questions.question: What is the most generally used indicator of overall economic performance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Per capita Gross National Product**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Per capita Gross National Product** is the most generally used indicator of **overall economic performance**.
 
• Per capita Gross National Product (GNP) is indeed a widely used indicator to gauge the economic performance of a country.
 
• It measures the average economic output per person in a given country, providing insight into the standard of living and economic well-being of its citizens.
 
• By dividing the total GNP of a country by its population, policymakers, economists, and analysts can assess trends in economic growth, compare the economic performance of different countries, and make informed decisions regarding economic policies and strategies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Human Development Index (HDI)** indeed serves as a comprehensive measure of a country's social and economic development, encompassing key factors like education, health, and income. By combining indicators such as mean years of schooling, expected years of schooling, life expectancy at birth, and gross national income (GNI) per capita, the HDI provides a holistic assessment of human well-being and development across different nations.
 
• **The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI)** offers another perspective on societal well-being by considering various social factors, including life expectancy, infant mortality rate, and literacy rate. It provides a broader understanding of the overall quality of life within a population, highlighting areas for improvement and policy intervention.
 
• **The standard of living** refers to the overall level of prosperity and well-being enjoyed by individuals or communities, typically measured by factors such as income, access to basic needs, and quality of life indicators. It provides insight into the material comforts, services, and opportunities available to people within a given society or location, reflecting their economic and social status.

questions.question: The analysis of the interrelationship between the economy and the environment in the economic environmental accounting system was put forward by ______.
questions.solution:

• The analysis of the interrelationship between **the economy and the environment in the economic environmental accounting system** was put forward by** ****United Nations Statistical Office**.
 
• The System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA), endorsed by the United Nations Statistical Commission in 2012, serves as the official international framework for natural capital accounting.
 
• It offers a standardized approach to organizing and presenting statistics concerning the environment and its interconnectedness with the economy.
 
• At its core, SEEA comprises two key components: the Central Framework (SEEA-CF) and Ecosystems Accounting (SEEA-EA).
 
• The SEEA-CF adopts an economic perspective, analyzing how natural resources such as fish, timber, and water are utilized in production and consumption processes.
 
• Additionally, it examines the resultant pollution, encompassing waste, water, and air emissions. On the other hand, SEEA-EA complements the Central Framework by focusing on ecosystems and their significance in enhancing human well-being through the provision of identifiable ecosystem services.
 
• This component offers insights into the contribution of ecosystems to various aspects of human life, offering a holistic understanding of environmental sustainability and economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **The Central Statistics Office (CSO)** is a governmental agency in India operating under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. Its primary responsibilities include coordinating statistical activities across India and developing and upholding statistical standards.
 
• **The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI)** in Nagpur, originally established in 1958 as the Central Public Health Engineering Research Institute (CPHERI), focuses on research and development in the field of environmental engineering.
 
• **DES** serves as the Principal Statistical Organisation of the State Government, overseeing all statistical activities within the state. It is designated as the "Nodal Agency" responsible for coordinating statistical endeavors throughout the state.
